qualifications: Three distinct income views are kept separate and must not be interchanged: (a) T12 historical (Sep-2025 to Aug-2026): EGI 821,100 / NOI before reserves 513,300 / NCF 502,500; (b) point-in-time contractual rent at 2026-08-31: 62,275/month = 747,300 annualized; (c) supplied underwriting scenario (Sep-2026 forward): EGI 854,160 / NOI before reserves 545,960 / NCF 535,160.

Unreconciled evidence, disclosed rather than forced: the underwriting GPR of $864,000 (Property-and-Plan.pdf p.2) exceeds both T12 actual GPR of $840,000 (T12-Statement.pdf p.2) and the rent roll's total gross potential at market rents ($68,300/month x 12 = $819,600, i.e., 36 units at $1,675/$2,175). The plan states this GPR is a supplied scenario 'not inferred from the T12', and Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1 instructs that historical income not be forced to a point-in-time annualized rent roll. The $44,400 (5.4%) gap above rent-roll market potential is a flagged underwriting risk, not a reconciled fact.

Label caution honored: Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1 warns the accounting package may call after-reserve cash flow 'property NOI'. NOI before reserves and NCF after reserves are reported separately for both T12 and underwritten cases.

T12 operating expenses exclude replacement reserves (10,800), capital improvements (62,000), loan principal and interest (294,000) and depreciation (180,000) per the T12 footnotes and Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1.

The management-fee floor binds in both the base case and the -5% EGI stress: 3% of EGI (25,625 base / 24,344 stress) is below the T12 actual of 30,000, so no expense relief is credited in the downside.

Rate distinction: contract rate 5.90% governs actual first-year debt service (all of year 1 falls inside the 24-month IO period, so year-1 DS is interest-only at 341,872); sizing rate 6.25% (the underwriting floor, which exceeds the contract rate) governs the DSCR test on a 30-year amortizing basis (428,128). The 86,256 gap between actual and sizing DS is a structural cushion, and amortization begins in month 25 (an approx. 86k annual step-up in required payments, before any refinancing at maturity in month 84).

Separate cap-rate sensitivity (workbook requirement, computed here): at 6.25% cap (+50 bps, base EGI) value = 545,960 / 0.0625 = 8,735,360; LTV limit = 5,677,984, which falls BELOW the DSCR limit of 5,794,436 - the binding constraint switches from DSCR to LTV and the maximum loan falls to 5,677,984 (-116,452). Cash to borrower would fall to approx. 2,290,400.

Lease/tenant profile: 36 residential units, 33 occupied (91.67% by count; 91.04% by area), 3 vacant (109, 125, 136). Vacant units carry market rent for context only and no contractual base rent (Rent-Roll.xlsx C45). Rollover is heavy and near-term: 6 leases expire on or before 2026-12-31 and effectively the entire rent roll expires within the 12 months following the as-of date, versus an 84-month loan term - a material re-leasing/rollover risk given the underwriting's 6.00% combined revenue-loss allowance. Unit 101 is the only lease with document-level evidence; the other 32 occupied units are supported by the rent roll alone.

Value is an indicative capitalization result only; Lender-Terms.pdf p.1 states no appraisal is implied, and Property-and-Plan.pdf p.1 confirms no appraisal, environmental report, sponsor track record, market comparables or completed credit approval was supplied. No market, sponsor or lender claims beyond the packet are made.

Sizing used unrounded intermediates per Lender-Terms.pdf p.1; displayed currency is rounded for readability. Debt-constant precision affects the last few dollars of the DSCR-driven limits (base approx. +/- $50; stress approx. +/- $100).

Term sheet is expressly nonbinding discussion terms dated 2026-09-01; no fee capitalization, interest reserve, cash sweep, earn-out or holdback assumed. This analysis is internal-review underwriting, not a legal opinion or credit commitment.
